correctness.rationale: Every nonalgebraic complete one-type is precisely a Katetov vector of distances 1..D to named parameters. For equilateral parameter distance s, a vector is valid iff width<=s and its two least values sum to at least s. Partitioning by minimum m yields the exact disjoint high/low summation. The maximal high width w and its multiplicity h are computed exactly; the largest low width coincides with w precisely for odd s>=3 and s<=D<=(3s-1)/2. This proves both asymptotic regimes and the probability transition. The proof treats boundary cases s=1,2 and n=1. The packaged independent brute-force algorithm matched all 210 finite cases and 120 large-n phase tests; those tests corroborate rather than substitute for proof.

originality.rationale: The new statement is the full equilateral (D,s,n) exact enumeration with its sharp parity/ambient-diameter phase boundary and concentration result. Sauer gives necessary and sufficient Katetov inequalities and finite metric homogeneity, but not a type-count formula or growth phase diagram. The closest published diameter-three result counts a graph-metric slice with distance-1/2 parameters and gives the general {1,2,3} triangle table, not the arbitrary D,s result; earlier finite-star metric tuple spectra involve a hub and fixed D=3. value.rationale: Equilateral sets are the canonical maximally symmetric finite parameter configurations in integer Urysohn spaces. The exact nonalgebraic one-type count is a natural family invariant, and the theorem determines it for every parameter distance and ambient diameter, not an arbitrary finite slice. Against the established #P-completeness of finite-parameter type counting on a graph-metric slice of the diameter-three limit, the exact equilateral family supplies a structured solvable reference case. The sharp if-and-only-if odd-distance phase separates concentration on a uniquely close landmark and a polynomial-times-exponential growth law from purely exponential growth and vanishing short-distance probability. This distinction can organize further finite-parameter type-growth investigations; no downstream conjecture is claimed proved.
